clue.text: A fragment from William Blake?

indicators.note: fragment from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A quizmaster asks for a snippet of verse by the Romantic poet William Blake.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'A' alone as the definition, which cannot define a metrical foot; the whole clue is the definition, since a single foot of verse is itself a fragment of a poem, and the letters sit inside WillIAM Blake.
explanation.definitionFit: A metrical foot of one short and one long syllable is a tiny unit of a poem, so it is literally a fragment of Blake's verse.

clue.text: Mischievous tendency that could make mess in ship

indicators.note: could make means the letters can be rearranged to form something new

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A naughty streak might cause chaos aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mess' looks like a ship's dining room, but it is anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Impishness is playful naughtiness, a tendency to mischief.

clue.text: Mark keeps embrace short for males in the family

indicators.note: keeps means holding another piece inside

parts.note: Mk is the abbreviation of mark

indicators.note: short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to enfold is to embrace

explanation.surface: Mark gives a quick hug to the men of his family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a man's name, which suits the family surface, but it is the abbreviation; 'short' trims the last letter of the embrace word.
explanation.definitionFit: Menfolk are the men of a family or community.

clue.text: Switching electricity provider is spreading a cost, or inviting trouble in

indicators.note: inviting trouble in means letting another piece come inside
spreading means the letters of a cost and or are spread out and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
ill as a noun means trouble or harm
taken as written

explanation.surface: A consumer changing energy supplier spreads the bills, or invites problems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Switching electricity provider' reads as changing your energy company, but it defines a device that makes current alternate. 'Spreading' turns A COST into OSCAT, and 'inviting' puts the trouble inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An oscillator is an electronic circuit producing an alternating current, so it provides electricity that switches direction.

clue.text: Undisturbed, note head of gnu entering Tanzanian park

indicators.note: entering means one piece goes inside another

parts.note: serene means calm and undisturbed

indicators.note: head of means the first letter is used

parts.note: ti is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A calm wildebeest wanders into an African game reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of gnu' gives G, which goes into the middle of the calm word plus the sol-fa note.
explanation.definitionFit: The Serengeti is a famous national park in northern Tanzania.

clue.text: Conclude superior should take head down a couple of pegs

indicators.text: take head down a couple of pegs
indicators.note: the first letter is moved two places further along the word

parts.note: finer means superior

explanation.surface: A subordinate decides the boss should be humbled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take down a peg' usually means humble; here F, the head of FINER, moves down two places.
explanation.definitionFit: To infer is to deduce or conclude from evidence.

clue.text: Organist? Golly, that's stretching it!

indicators.note: stretching it suggests the letters are pulled about into a new shape

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that calling a person an organist is an exaggeration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organist' is read as a specialist in an organ, here the voice box, so a throat doctor fits, and the clue's own letters rearrange to give it.
explanation.definitionFit: A laryngologist is a doctor specialising in the larynx, an organ, so whimsically an organ-ist.

clue.text: Heroic figure's article on location of Florida

parts.note: the is the definite article
Florida lies in the south-east, SE, of the United States, US

explanation.surface: A newspaper article celebrates a hero from Florida.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', linking definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Theseus is the hero of Greek myth who slew the Minotaur.

clue.text: Hotel has legal papers for auditor

indicators.note: for auditor means for a listener, so the sound counts

parts.note: writs are formal legal documents

explanation.surface: A hotel has legal documents prepared for its accountant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'auditor' suggests an accountant, but means a hearer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ritz is a famous luxury hotel in London and elsewhere.

clue.text: Basket that's more like a bowl, you might think

definitions.meaning: a basket carried on a bike or a beast of burden

definitions.text: more like a bowl, you might think
definitions.meaning: a pan is a bowl, and a comparative adjective of pan would be pan-ier, more pan-like

explanation.surface: Someone describes a basket as rather bowl-shaped.
explanation.definitionFit: A pannier is a large basket slung on a horse, donkey or bicycle for carrying goods.

clue.text: Domestic accepting reduced bonus, thus — that's just between you and me

indicators.note: accepting means taking another piece in

parts.note: internal means domestic, within a country

indicators.note: reduced means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a perk is a bonus
so means thus

explanation.surface: A domestic servant takes a smaller bonus, and asks to keep it quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' drops the last letter of the bonus word; 'Domestic' is an adjective meaning internal, not a household servant.
explanation.definitionFit: Interpersonal describes what passes between people, such as between you and me.

clue.text: Hot iron run by slit in garment

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run
a vent is a slit at the back or side of a jacket

explanation.surface: A tailor's hot iron passes along the slit in a jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot iron' looks like one tool, but 'Hot' is the definition and 'iron' gives FE.
explanation.definitionFit: Fervent means passionate or ardent, figuratively hot in feeling.

clue.text: Leave money with farmstead where targets are set

parts.note: shoo is what you say to tell someone to leave
tin is old slang for money
a grange is a farmhouse with its outbuildings

explanation.surface: A farmer quits with cash and the farm, now the site for target practice.
explanation.definitionFit: A shooting range is a place laid out for firing at targets.

clue.text: Commercial producer takes up second test with minister and prosecutor

indicators.note: takes up in a down clue means the whole string is read upwards

parts.note: a resit is an exam taken a second time
Rev is short for reverend, a minister
DA is a district attorney, an American prosecutor

explanation.surface: A TV producer takes on a retake with a cleric and a lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commercial' is a noun: a TV advert, whose producer is an advertiser.
explanation.definitionFit: An advertiser is the firm behind a commercial, the one who creates and pays for it.

clue.text: Showing more skin when edition goes out —- there could be a tattoo on it

definitions.text: there could be a tattoo on it

indicators.note: goes out means these letters are dropped from the word

parts.note: more naked, a comparative of naked

explanation.surface: A risqué magazine edition shows more flesh, including a tattoo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tattoo' looks like skin art, but here it is a drumbeat, so a naker, an old kettledrum, can have one played on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A naker is a medieval kettledrum, and a tattoo is a rhythmic drumbeat that could be beaten on one.

clue.text: Consumed English traditional Sunday dinner while talking

indicators.note: while talking means the words are heard spoken, not read

parts.note: Eng is short for English and a roast is the traditional British Sunday dinner

explanation.surface: Someone tucks into a traditional English Sunday roast while chatting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Consumed' looks like eating, matching the dinner, but means absorbed. A Sunday roast is roasted meat with vegetables, a British family custom.
explanation.definitionFit: Consumed by something means wholly absorbed in it, the same sense as being deeply engaged.

clue.text: Shoot head off pests coming through entrance

indicators.note: coming through means placed inside

parts.note: a gate is an entrance

indicators.note: head off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: vermin are pests

explanation.surface: A gamekeeper shoots the pests coming through the gate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoot' looks like gunfire, but means sprout.
explanation.definitionFit: To germinate is to sprout or put out shoots, as a seed does.

clue.text: One removes a capsule before opening battle that is between the usual sides

definitions.text: One removes a capsule before opening

parts.note: the Somme was a First World War battle

indicators.note: between says one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: L and R stand for left and right, the usual sides
ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A soldier unpacks a capsule before the start of a battle fought between familiar sides.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'capsule' is the foil cap over a wine bottle's cork, not a military item.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine waiter cuts away the foil cap on a bottle before drawing the cork and serving.

clue.text: Dames in development?

indicators.note: development suggests letters being worked into a new form

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Grand ladies at an early stage of their growth.
explanation.definitionFit: Maidens are young girls, women in the making who will grow into dames.

clue.text: In maturity, one's waist going out? A wearisome task to replace it

indicators.note: the waist of a word is its middle letter, which goes out to make room

parts.note: taken as written, the possessive adding no letter
a fag is British slang for a tiresome chore

explanation.surface: Someone ageing notices their waistline expanding, a tiresome thing to fix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to replace it' tells you FAG replaces the middle letter N of ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being of age means being legally adult, having reached the age of maturity.

clue.text: Bachelor in solitary confinement? One lives in a shell

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: alone means by oneself, in solitary
BA is Bachelor of Arts

explanation.surface: A single man locked in solitary lives like a creature in a shell.
explanation.definitionFit: An abalone is an edible sea snail living in an ear-shaped shell.

clue.text: Meaningless popular gesture, be it impossible for me

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a sign is a gesture
if I can't, written without its apostrophe, means should it be impossible for me

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a popular gesture as pointless if they can't manage it.
explanation.definitionFit: Insignificant means trivial or of no importance, having no meaning.

clue.text: A vine's first month climbing tropical tree

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means read upwards
first picks out the initial letter

parts.note: Aug is the abbreviation for August

explanation.surface: A vine climbs a tropical tree in its first month.
explanation.definitionFit: The guava is a tropical tree grown for its fruit.

clue.text: Planet's core has gone down

indicators.note: core has gone means the middle letter is removed

parts.note: the world is our planet

explanation.surface: A planet's core has sunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' looks like a verb, but is a noun: open upland.
explanation.definitionFit: A wold is open rolling upland, the same as downs or downland.

clue.text: One needs a canoe, navigating around a lot of islands

indicators.note: around means this piece goes round the other one
navigating suggests the letters steer a new course into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A traveller needs a canoe to paddle round a group of islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'navigating' turns A CANOE into OCEAN plus A, and 'around' wraps those letters round I.
explanation.definitionFit: Oceania is the region made up of the many islands of the Pacific, including Australasia.

clue.text: Writes to the French, yet rejects going to extremes

parts.note: au is French for to the
tho, short for though, means yet

indicators.note: going to extremes means only the outermost letters are taken

explanation.surface: A writer submits to French publishers, yet faces rejections at every turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going to extremes' takes the first and last letters of 'rejects'.
explanation.definitionFit: To author a book is to write it, so the verb form matches writes.

clue.text: Angry and insulted when appeal is squashed

indicators.note: is squashed means this piece is pressed inside the other

parts.note: dissed is slang for insulted
a plea is an appeal

explanation.surface: A petitioner is furious and offended when their appeal is crushed.
explanation.definitionFit: Displeased means annoyed or angry with someone.

clue.text: Taunt clown heartlessly

indicators.note: heartlessly means the central letters are cut out

parts.note: a jester is a court clown

explanation.surface: Someone mocks a clown cruelly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' removes ST, the middle of JESTER.
explanation.definitionFit: To jeer is to mock or taunt loudly.
